tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create ONE new test file. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls. Do NOT edit any production code.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, fewer than 4 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILE (only this, new):
  tests/test_no_orphan_modules.py

WHY. This repo's recurring defect class: a capability is built, tested, and never wired
— it emits no signal, so every audit rediscovers it. A static scan this week found 12 of
102 server/pipeline modules with no caller, including two built THAT WEEK to fix this
exact problem. The owner's rule: an unused module either has a caller, a DAG step, or an
explicit on-the-record reason. This test is the enforcement.

BUILD tests/test_no_orphan_modules.py:
  * Static import scan, stdlib only (ast). For every module server/pipeline/<name>.py
    (skip __init__), find REAL callers: any module under server/ or scripts/ (tests/ do
    NOT count as callers) whose AST imports it (`import server.pipeline.<name>`,
    `from server.pipeline import <name>`, `from server.pipeline.<name> import ...`,
    including aliased forms). Entry points don't need callers: a module with a
    `if __name__ == "__main__"` block that is referenced by name from any file under
    scripts/ or scripts/systemd/ (string match in .sh/.service/.timer files counts)
    is considered called.
  * A module with zero callers must appear in the explicit ALLOWLIST dict in this test
    file: {module_name: reason}. Reasons must be honest one-liners. Seed the allowlist
    by RUNNING your scan and triaging every current orphan: a module that one of this
    week's changes wired (check the scan result, do not assume) must NOT be
    allowlisted; a genuinely unwired module gets a reason of the form
    "known-orphan (AUDIT-2026-07-31): <why it exists / what should wire it>".
  * test_no_unexplained_orphans: scan set minus called set minus allowlist == empty,
    with a failure message that names each offender and says how to fix it (wire it,
    delete it, or allowlist it WITH a reason).
  * test_allowlist_is_not_stale: every allowlisted module (a) still exists and (b)
    still has zero callers — a wired module must be REMOVED from the allowlist so the
    list never rots into a bypass.
  * test_scan_finds_known_wiring (positive control): assert the scanner sees at least
    one known-true caller edge, e.g. that server.pipeline.post_prep is imported by
    something under server/ or scripts/ — proving the scanner itself works (a scanner
    that finds nothing would otherwise pass everything).
  * NEGATIVE control test: run the scanner over a tmp tree you construct in the test
    with a deliberately orphaned module and assert it is detected — the check must be
    able to fail.
  * Deterministic: sort everything; no filesystem-order dependence.
tasks.verified: a pipeline module with no caller and no on-the-record reason now fails the suite — unused capability can no longer hide
